question: Which of the following household items does NOT use the heating effect of current?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric motor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy, not heat.
 
• Electric stoves, water heaters, and iron boxes use the heating effect of current to function.
 
• In electric stoves, the current passes through resistive heating elements, generating heat.
 
• Electric water heaters use heating elements that convert electrical energy into heat to warm water.
 
• Electric iron boxes have resistive elements that produce heat to iron clothes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heating Elements**

 
 
• They are made of materials with high resistivity, such as nichrome, which converts electrical energy into heat efficiently.
 
• Commonly used in household appliances like toasters, hair dryers, and space heaters.
 
 
 
• **Resistive Heating**
 
 
• This is the process by which an electric current passes through a resistive material, causing it to heat up.
 
• It is widely used in various applications, including industrial heating and household appliances.
 
 
 
• **Electric Motors**
 
 
• They are used in a wide range of applications, from household appliances to industrial machinery.
 
• Electric motors work based on electromagnetic induction and do not primarily rely on the heating effect of current.
